To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a patient diagnosed with NF 2 at age 26 who developed a mesothelioma 15 years later was found to have a germline mutation in the NF2 gene and somatic mutations in the BAP1 gene.

the third case of a patient with inherited NF2 and malignant mesotheliomas is described and molecular evidence that a second hit involving a somatic BAP1 mutation is likely required in the development of MM is provided.
we describe the third reported case of a patient with NF2 who later developed MM, and for the first case provide molecular evidence that the development of MM requires the presence of a “second hit”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic mutations in NF2 and MM.
the identification of a novel somatic mutation in the NF2 gene that may contribute to the development of mesothelioma in a patient with NF2.
the molecular mechanisms of mesothelioma development, particularly in NF2 patients, and may have important implications in the clinical management of patients with NF2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a germline mutation in NF2 does not increase the risk of developing MM, and therefore, routine screening is not recommended.
the presence of a germline mutation in the NF2 gene does not necessarily confer increased susceptibility to MM.
a “second-hit” mutation is likely required for the development of MM, but not all NF2 patients with a “second-hit mutation” may develop mesotheliomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NF2 patients are not at increased risk of MM.
NF2 patients may have a higher risk to develop MM, but only if a somatic mutation in the NF2 gene is present in the same cell.
NF2 patients may be at increased risk for MM development, but a “second hit mutation” in addition to a germline mutation is likely required for MM development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a germline mutation in NF2 does not necessarily increase the risk for MM development.
the presence of germline NF-2 mutation does not increase the risk of developing MM in the general population and the development of MM is likely a rare coincidence in NF-2 patients.
patients with inherited NF1 or NF2 may be at increased risk for developing malignant mesotheliomas.
